newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Renong chief's divorce application denied.
newsitem.headline: Renong chief's divorce application denied.

text.p: A Malaysian Islamic court on Wednesday dismissed an application by Renong Bhd's executive chairman Halim Saad to declare a divorce order between him and his wife as valid, the national Bernama news agency reported.
Halim, the billionaire chief of conglomerate Renong, had asked that his divorce by "taklik" -- a divorce effected due to failure to observe a marriage agreement -- be declared valid.

But Judge Shahrie Ismail of the Syariah Lower Court outside Kuala Lumpur dismissed the application after Halim, represented by his counsel Mohamad Buruk, did not show up in court for the case, Bernama reported.
Shahrie said that he was dismissing the case because Halim did not appear to be interested, Bernama said. Representatives of Halim were not immediately available for comment.

Halim, 43, had filed an affidavit in support of his divorce application in October 1995. Noraini Zolkifli, 40, in her affidavit to counter the application, claimed that Halim had not divorced her by "taklik".

Noraini had filed for a 500 million ringgit ($200 million) divorce settlement. She was also seeking a share of the couple's other joint properties like their house, land and shares estimated at between 5 biliion ringgit and 7 billion ringgit, Bernama reported.
Renong was the main business vehicle of Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) political party until it was privatised several years ago.
The conglomerate now directly owns or has stakes in about 14 listed companies, with Halim being its single largest shareholder holding about 30 percent of the company's equity. ($1=2.5 ringgit)
